name: EMMA
description: Enhanced MultiModal ReAsoning benchmark targets organic cross-modal reasoning across mathematics, physics, chemistry, and coding where tasks cannot be solved by reasoning independently within each modality — successful completion requires genuine integration of visual and textual information. Reveals significant limitations even with Chain-of-Thought and test-time compute scaling, suggesting current multimodal models lack true cross-modal synthesis.
typical_sota_score: ~20–35% (frontier multimodal models; CoT and test-time scaling provide limited improvement)
reputation: ICML 2025 Oral (one of only 120 oral papers); from Microsoft Research; addresses a fundamental limitation in multimodal evaluation by requiring genuine cross-modal integration rather than text-or-image-alone solvability
notes: ICML 2025 Oral (one of 120 oral papers from thousands of submissions). EMMA's core design principle: every problem requires information from both visual and textual modalities — neither alone is sufficient. This filters out problems that multimodal models might solve by ignoring vision. Covers 4 STEM domains. Finding: even o1-level reasoning with image inputs fails significantly, and test-time compute scaling that dramatically helps text-only tasks provides limited benefit on EMMA.
